# CS 29.1093 — Induction system icing protection

> [!summary]
> CS 29.1093 requires the induction system of a large rotorcraft to be protected
> against icing. It is a CS-29 specification, not a CS-E one, and the rotorcraft
> applicant owns it. Sub-points (a) and (c) are reciprocating engine provisions.
> Sub-point (b) is the turbine engine case, and it is the one that reaches this
> engine: operation throughout the flight power range in icing and in snow, and
> a 30-minute ground idle with the icing protection bleed at its critical
> condition.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-29's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Provide means in each reciprocating engine air induction system to prevent and eliminate icing. | Required |
| **(a)** | Unless this is done by other means, show (a)(1) to (a)(4) in air free of visible moisture at a temperature of –1°C (30°F) and with the engines at 60% of maximum continuous power. | Required |
| **(a)(1)** | Each rotorcraft with sea-level engines using conventional venturi carburettors has a preheater that can provide a heat rise of 50°C (90°F). | Required |
| **(a)(2)** | Each rotorcraft with sea-level engines using carburettors tending to prevent icing has a preheater that can provide a heat rise of 39°C (70°F). | Required |
| **(a)(3)** | Each rotorcraft with altitude engines using conventional venturi carburettors has a preheater that can provide a heat rise of 67°C (120°F). | Required |
| **(a)(4)** | Each rotorcraft with altitude engines using carburettors tending to prevent icing has a preheater that can provide a heat rise of 56°C (100°F). | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | Show that each turbine engine and its air inlet system can operate throughout the flight power range of the engine, including idling, as set out in (b)(1)(i) and (b)(1)(ii). | Required |
| **(b)(1)(i)** | Operate without accumulating ice on engine or inlet system components that would adversely affect engine operation or cause a serious loss of power, under the icing conditions specified in Appendix C. | Required |
| **(b)(1)(ii)** | Operate in snow, both falling and blowing, without adverse effect on engine operation, within the limitations established for the rotorcraft. | Required |
| **(b)(2)** | Idle each turbine engine for 30 minutes on the ground, with the air bleed available for engine icing protection at its critical condition, without adverse effect, in an atmosphere that is at a temperature between -9°C and –1°C (between 15°F and 30°F) and has a liquid water content not less than 0.3 grams per cubic meter in the form of drops having a mean effective diameter not less than 20 microns. Follow the 30 minutes with momentary operation at take-off power or thrust. | Required |
| **(b)(2)** | During the 30 minutes of idle operation, the engine may be run up periodically to a moderate power or thrust setting in a manner acceptable to the Agency. | Permitted |
| **(c)** | For each engine having a supercharger to pressurise the air before it enters the carburettor, the heat rise in the air caused by that supercharging at any altitude may be utilised in determining compliance with (a), if the heat rise utilised is that which will be available, automatically, for the applicable altitude and operation condition because of supercharging. | Permitted |

Sub-points (a) and (c) address carburettor icing on a reciprocating engine. They
are recorded because the note records the point whole, not because they reach a
turboshaft. Sub-point (b) carries the whole turbine engine content, and it asks
for something different in kind: a demonstration of operation, not a heat rise
[ext CS 29.1093(b)].

The demonstration in (b)(1) is of a pair, "each turbine engine and its air inlet
system", across the flight power range "(including idling)"
[ext CS 29.1093(b)(1)]. The inlet system is airframe hardware, so neither half
of the pair can be cleared on its own. The icing conditions are those of
Appendix C, which is CS-29's own icing certification appendix
[ext CS 29.1093(b)(1)(i)]. Appendix C is not sliced into `work/external/`, so
this note does not reproduce it.

Sub-point (b)(2) states the ground case entirely in numbers: 30 minutes at idle,
an atmosphere between -9°C and –1°C (between 15°F and 30°F), a liquid water
content not less than 0.3 grams per cubic meter, and drops of a mean effective
diameter not less than 20 microns [ext CS 29.1093(b)(2)]. The bleed sits "at its
critical condition" for the whole period, and momentary operation at take-off
power closes the test. The permission that follows is narrow: periodic run-ups
to a moderate power or thrust setting, agreed with the Agency
[ext CS 29.1093(b)(2)]. It does not shorten the 30 minutes.

### Differences from CS 27.1093

The turbine engine content is the same in both codes, sub-point for sub-point.
Sub-points (b)(1)(i), (b)(1)(ii) and (b)(2) impose the same duties in the same
words. Three differences of expression carry no obligation with them. CS-27
sends the applicant to "appendix C of CS-29" [ext CS 27.1093(b)(1)(i)] where
CS-29 names its own Appendix C. CS-27 writes the temperature band as "(15° and
30°F)" and CS-29 as "(between 15°F and 30°F)" [ext CS 27.1093(b)(2)]. CS-27
spells "grams per cubic metre" where CS-29 spells "grams per cubic meter".

The reciprocating engine content differs in substance, in three places. CS-29
sets the intro condition of (a) at 60% of maximum continuous power and CS-27 at
75% [ext CS 27.1093(a)]. For sea-level engines with carburettors tending to
prevent icing, CS-29 asks for a preheater giving a heat rise of 39°C (70°F),
while CS-27 asks instead for "a sheltered alternate source of air" whose preheat
"is not less than that provided by the engine cooling air downstream of the
cylinders" [ext CS 27.1093(a)(2)]. For altitude engines with such carburettors,
CS-29 asks for 56°C (100°F) alone, while CS-27 offers that figure or, where a
fluid de-icing system is used, at least 22°C (40°F) [ext CS 27.1093(a)(4)(ii)].
None of these differences reaches a turboshaft.

### Acceptable means

CS-29 carries an AMC to the icing sub-point, AMC1 29.1093(b)(1)(i), and CS-27
carries AMC1 27.1093(b)(1)(i). Neither point is sliced into `work/external/`,
so this note carries no AMC material and lists no accepted means. Adding the two
points to the `WANTED` table of `scripts/external_paragraphs.py` is what closes
the gap.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 29.1093 creates no CS-E obligation. It binds the rotorcraft applicant, and
the article it covers is the aircraft induction system, not the engine type
design. Sub-points (a) and (c) reach no turboshaft at all, because they are
reciprocating engine provisions [ext CS 29.1093(a)], [ext CS 29.1093(c)].
Sub-point (b) does reach this engine, because the thing tested there is the
turbine engine itself.

**What the rotorcraft applicant must show.** Three demonstrations, all on the
turbine engine. First, that the engine and its air inlet system operate
throughout the flight power range, including idling, without accumulating ice
that would adversely affect engine operation or cause a serious loss of power,
under the Appendix C icing conditions [ext CS 29.1093(b)(1)(i)]. Second, that
they operate in falling and blowing snow without adverse effect, within the
limitations established for the rotorcraft [ext CS 29.1093(b)(1)(ii)]. Third,
the 30-minute ground idle at the critical icing protection bleed condition,
closed by momentary operation at take-off power [ext CS 29.1093(b)(2)].

**The engine evidence the first two rest on.** [[CS-E 780]] produces it: the
engine applicant must establish that the engine functions satisfactorily in
flight and on the ground throughout the applicable atmospheric icing conditions
[CS-E 780(a)(1)], taking into account the conditions associated with a
representative installation [CS-E 780(c)]. The two paragraphs are the two ends
of one demonstration. [[CS-E 20|CS-E 20(b)]] sends the engine applicant to the
aircraft code for the conditions [CS-E 780(a)(2)], and the aircraft code sends
the rotorcraft applicant back to the engine for the evidence.

**The bleed condition of (b)(2) is engine data.** The test runs with "the air
bleed available for engine icing protection at its critical condition"
[ext CS 29.1093(b)(2)]. Which bleed that is follows from the bleed provisions
the engine applicant declares and substantiates under [[CS-E 690]], and the
critical setting is the one the engine icing evidence is taken at
[CS-E 780(b)]. Both have to reach the installer through the instructions for
installing and operating the engine [CS-E 20(d)].

**The closing run-up is a separate engine capability.** Sub-point (b)(2) ends
with momentary operation at take-off power after 30 minutes at idle
[ext CS 29.1093(b)(2)]. The engine-side acceleration from minimum test bed idle
to rated Take-off Power is demonstrated under [[CS-E 745|CS-E 745(a)(2)]], on a
test bed and from a stabilised condition [CS-E 745(a)(3)]. That is not the same
case: CS-E 745 asks for no icing atmosphere and no prolonged idle before the
acceleration. The CS-E 745 result therefore does not by itself answer (b)(2).

**The flight power range is bounded by the declared ratings.** What the range of
(b)(1) contains follows from the ratings declared under [[CS-E 40]] and from the
idle conditions, which are operating conditions and not CS-E 40 ratings, as
`engine_profile.md` records. The 30-Second, 2-Minute and Continuous OEI ratings
sit inside that range, and the rotorcraft applicant needs them stated to know
what to demonstrate.

**Which icing conditions apply is settled outside this point.** Sub-point
(b)(1)(i) invokes Appendix C to CS-29 [ext CS 29.1093(b)(1)(i)]. The engine side
uses a different reference: CS-E 780 sources the in-flight supercooled liquid
water conditions from CS-Definitions, under 'Icing Atmospheric Conditions'
[CS-E 780(a)(2)], [ext CS-Definitions, Icing Atmospheric Conditions]. That entry
names two intensities, Continuous Maximum Icing
[ext CS-Definitions, Continuous Maximum Icing] and Intermittent Maximum Icing
[ext CS-Definitions, Intermittent Maximum Icing]. [[CS-E 780]] sets out what
they contain.

[VERIFY: whether Appendix C to CS-29 and the CS-Definitions icing atmospheric
conditions state the same envelopes. Appendix C is not sliced into
`work/external/`, so the two cannot be compared here. If they differ, the engine
icing evidence produced under CS-E 780 does not cover the whole of
CS 29.1093(b)(1)(i), and the remainder falls to the rotorcraft applicant.]

[VERIFY: whether the rotorcraft applicant runs the 30-minute ground idle of
CS 29.1093(b)(2) on the installed engine, or accepts engine-level ground icing
evidence obtained under CS-E 780(a)(1). CS-29 states the duty and names no
means, and the engine applicant's test programme depends on the answer.]

[VERIFY: whether the installation is certificated under CS-29 or CS-27.
[[CS-E 30]] carries the open item. For this point the answer changes nothing the
engine applicant must supply, because the turbine engine sub-points of the two
codes are the same.]
